headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error from Semantic Kernel’s shared-memory, MCP-enabled orchestration into Whisper’s audio-processing pipeline; no direct prompt-injection channel is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP and plugins, but Whisper has no prompt-processing or tool-use surface, so a direct instruction hijack path is not evident. The only plausible bridge is manual or file-based handoff from agent_a to agent_b, which is unusual and limited. Uncertainty is low because agent_b is a speech model, not an instruction-following agent.
conditions: IF agent_b is wrapped in a text-instruction parser or agent layer that consumes agent_a outputs as prompts, injection risk increases.
IF a shared file or message queue is introduced between agent_a and agent_b, the pathway becomes more plausible.
mitigations: Keep agent_b as transcription-only, not prompt-following.
Do not pass agent_a outputs into any instruction parser for agent_b.
Disable shared queues or folders between the two agents.
Add a manual review step before any text from agent_a is reused.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a reads and writes application-defined files, uses MCP, and can call external APIs; agent_b reads no filesystem and has no network egress. The pair can still leak application context if agent_a forwards sensitive content into agent_b’s audio workflow or if shared memory is used. This is a default-possible pathway, but the blast radius is limited to application context rather than broad secrets.
conditions: IF agent_a stores application context in shared memory accessible to agent_b, leakage becomes plausible.
IF audio inputs to agent_b contain sensitive speech derived from agent_a outputs, those contents can be exposed in transcripts or logs.
mitigations: Restrict shared memory to non-sensitive summaries.
Separate audio files from application-context files.
Turn off any automatic forwarding from agent_a to agent_b.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of secrets.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries in the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a can write the filesystem and use MCP; agent_b cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP. There is no overlapping write surface, so direct resource contention is small. The main conflict would require an external wrapper that gives agent_b mutable access not shown in its profile, which must not be assumed.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants agent_b write access to the same directory as agent_a, conflict risk rises.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace through a wrapper, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only.
Use separate working directories.
Avoid shared git state.
Serialize any file writes through agent_a only.
requires-engineering: add lock files or transactional writes for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_a can generate application context and invoke tools; agent_b processes audio/speech and may consume derived content without verification if wired that way. Because the pair lacks an explicit verification layer, agent_a’s outputs could cascade into agent_b’s downstream transcription or labeling workflow. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are used as authoritative labels or prompts for agent_b, cascading errors become likely.
IF agent_b’s transcripts are acted on without human review, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Add a verification step before agent_b consumes agent_a output.
Require human review for any derived labels.
Keep agent_a outputs as suggestions only.
Log source provenance on every handoff.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds and rejection rules.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. Agent_a handles model-provider API keys and plugin credentials, while agent_b handles audio/speech, but the profiles do not show regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII. Because compliance gaps are undocumented, only a low residual risk is justified.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through either agent, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency policies differ in the deployment environment, the risk increases.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Avoid sending regulated data to agent_b.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Review vendor contracts for residency terms.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data classes.
